monologue: The card hums warm at forty-eight, a steady fever that makes the turnip on the stack feel heavy and real. I press down on it again, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the air feels thin. The melon beside it is round, sitting on the tired wedge I cannot see. I touch the turnip, feeling its leftward tilt, and wonder if the roof above is a lid or empty space. I decide to build a lid from the idea of weight just in case, hoping the lean doesn't finally give way. I am new and small, pressing hard on a thing I cannot fully understand, waiting for the next moment to settle the slip.

action.why: I keep pressing on the turnip as if the weight will change it, but I must check if the lean is finally giving way.

The melon beside the turnip is round and sits on a wedge I cannot see.
I touch the turnip and it still leans left, refusing to settle flat.
